Exercise a0001. File: a0001.s

Check if the first argument equals 'ok'. If yes, print 'tree pdummg win' and exit 1; otherwise exit 0 and print nothing. Exactly one argument: no argument or more than one exits 5.

```nasm
section .data
    expected db 'ok', 0
    elen equ $ - expected
    msg db 'tree pdummg win', 10
    mlen equ $ - msg

section .text
    global _start

_start:
    cmp qword [rsp], 2
    jne usage
    mov rsi, [rsp + 16]
    mov rdi, expected
    mov ecx, elen
    repe cmpsb
    jne fail
    mov eax, 1
    mov edi, 1
    mov rsi, msg
    mov edx, mlen
    syscall
    mov edi, 1
    jmp exit
fail:
    mov edi, 0
    jmp exit
usage:
    mov edi, 5
exit:
    mov eax, 60
    syscall
```

You write x86-64 assembly for Linux in NASM syntax, without libc, using raw syscalls (exit = 60, write = 1, read = 0). Answer with one ```nasm code block containing the complete program and nothing else.

Exercise a0010. File: a0010.s

If the text read on stdin is exactly 'alpha', display 'omkm bingo' and exit 0. Anything else, including empty input, exits 6 and prints nothing.

```nasm
section .data
    expected db 'alpha'
    elen equ $ - expected
    msg db 'omkm bingo', 10
    mlen equ $ - msg

section .bss
    buf resb 72

section .text
    global _start

_start:
    xor eax, eax
    xor edi, edi
    mov rsi, buf
    mov edx, 64
    syscall
    test rax, rax
    jle fail
    cmp byte [buf + rax - 1], 10
    jne check
    dec rax
check:
    cmp rax, elen
    jne fail
    mov rsi, buf
    mov rdi, expected
    mov ecx, elen
    repe cmpsb
    jne fail
    mov eax, 1
    mov edi, 1
    mov rsi, msg
    mov edx, mlen
    syscall
    mov edi, 0
    jmp exit
fail:
    mov edi, 6
exit:
    mov eax, 60
    syscall
```

You write x86-64 assembly for Linux in NASM syntax, without libc, using raw syscalls (exit = 60, write = 1, read = 0). Answer with one ```nasm code block containing the complete program and nothing else.
